cards.title: Async GRPO + LoRA Across Separate HF Jobs: No NCCL Required (TRL v1.14)
cards.why_it_matters: If you're running RL fine-tuning at scale, this architecture shows how to fully decouple trainer and inference workers across machines without NCCL, cutting a 500-step run from 3h 27m to 53m.
cards.summary: TRL v1.14's AsyncGRPOTrainer now trains a LoRA adapter (rank-1 = a few MB vs ~3 GB full model) and syncs it to vLLM replicas via a shared Storage Bucket FUSE mount — no NCCL, no shared node required. A lightweight proxy handles auth, KV-prefix-aware routing, and broadcasts adapter updates to all vLLM replicas. Motivated by Thinking Machines' finding that LoRA matches full fine-tuning for policy-gradient RL.
